title: The 'Burbs
about: A man spending his week off at home becomes convinced the strange new family next door are murderers.
cue: Pass the sardines when Carol marches the men next door to meet the Klopeks.
faces: to eat, laugh and watch a film at
Sardine? Bonnie's trying to cut back. Sardine toasts.

Art eats everything in Ray's fridge. Paprika yolks, crisp bacon, chives.
Take one. Ray did, and lived.
Rumsfield asks if Klopek is Slavic. Slow-cooked beef goulash.
Ricky called the pizza dude for the show. Pepperoni, mozzarella, chilli honey.
There go the brownies. Fudgy walnut brownies, salted caramel.
Hans makes the coffee. Mind your lap. Cold brew coffee floats.

    First CourseRoom-temperature sardines on ryeSardine? Bonnie's trying to cut back. Sardine toasts, lemon butter, pickled shallot.How to make it2 x 110g tins of sardines in olive oil8 slices of dark rye bread50g butter, softened1 lemon, zested and juiced2 shallots, thinly sliced60ml white wine vinegar1 tsp caster sugar1/2 cup dill sprigsWarm the vinegar with the sugar and a pinch of salt, pour over the shallots and leave to pickle.Mash the butter with the lemon zest and a pinch of pepper.Toast the rye and spread with the lemon butter.Lay the sardines on top, squeeze over a little lemon and finish with shallots and dill.Femur-cut roast bone marrowVince digs up a femur next door. Roast bone marrow on toast, caper salad.How to make it4 beef marrow bones, cut lengthways1 cup flat-leaf parsley leaves1 shallot, thinly sliced1 tbsp capers1 lemon1 tbsp olive oil1 sourdough baguette, sliced1 tsp sea salt flakesPat the bones dry, season and stand them cut side up on a tray.Roast at 220°C until the marrow is soft and just starting to bubble.Toss the parsley, shallot and capers with the oil and lemon juice.Toast the bread and serve with the bones, the salad and salt for scooping and spreading.Art's fridge-raid devilled eggsArt eats everything in Ray's fridge. Paprika yolks, crisp bacon, chives.How to make it8 eggs4 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 tsp Dijon mustard1 tsp cider vinegar1 tsp sweet paprika3 rashers of streaky bacon1 tbsp chives, snippedLower the eggs into boiling water, cook 10 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel.Fry the bacon until crisp, then crumble.Halve the eggs, mash the yolks with the mayo, mustard and vinegar and season well.Pipe or spoon back in and finish with paprika, bacon and chives.Salted pretzels in a bowlTake one. Ray did, and lived.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Main CourseHerr Klopek's paprika goulashRumsfield asks if Klopek is Slavic. Slow-cooked beef goulash, sour cream, noodles.How to make it1kg beef chuck, cut in chunks2 tbsp plain flour3 tbsp vegetable oil2 brown onions, sliced3 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp sweet paprika1 tsp caraway seeds2 tbsp tomato paste2 red capsicums, sliced750ml beef stock400g wide egg noodles30g butter150g sour cream2 tbsp parsley, choppedToss the beef in the flour and brown it hard in the oil in batches.Soften the onions and garlic in the same pot, then stir in the paprika, caraway and tomato paste for a minute.Return the beef with the capsicum and stock, cover and simmer gently until the beef falls apart.Boil the noodles, drain and toss with the butter and parsley.Serve the goulash over the noodles with a spoon of sour cream.Pizza dude pepperoni pieRicky called the pizza dude for the show. Pepperoni, mozzarella, chilli honey.How to make it2 x 400g balls of pizza dough400g tin crushed tomatoes1 garlic clove, crushed1 tsp dried oregano300g mozzarella, grated150g sliced pepperoni salami2 tbsp honey1 tsp chilli flakes30g parmesan, gratedMix the tomatoes, garlic, oregano and a pinch of salt for the sauce.Stretch the dough into 2 large rounds on oiled trays.Spread with sauce, cover with mozzarella and pepperoni and bake at 250°C until blistered.Warm the honey with the chilli, drizzle over and finish with parmesan.DessertRumsfield's porch browniesThere go the brownies. Fudgy walnut brownies, salted caramel.How to make it200g dark chocolate, chopped150g butter250g brown sugar3 eggs100g plain flour30g cocoa powder80g walnuts, toasted and chopped120g salted caramel sauce300ml thickened creamMelt the chocolate and butter, then beat in the sugar and the eggs one at a time.Fold in the flour, cocoa, walnuts and a pinch of salt and spread in a lined 20cm tin.Swirl spoonfuls of the caramel through the top and bake at 170°C until just set.Cool, cut into squares and serve with softly whipped cream.To ToastHans's iced coffee floatsHans makes the coffee. Mind your lap. Cold brew coffee floats, vanilla ice cream.How to make it500ml cold brew coffee250ml milk2 tbsp maple syrup8 scoops of vanilla ice cream150ml thickened cream, whipped1 tsp cocoa powder1 tray iceStir the cold brew, milk and maple syrup together.Half fill 4 tall glasses with ice and pour in the coffee.Float 2 scoops of ice cream in each, top with whipped cream and dust with cocoa.Cold beer on the front porchRay's on vacation. He's staying home.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
